The U.S. "Red Book" contains accounts of not only species and subspecies now considered threatened with extinction (endangered as defined by present authority) but also those for which special concern has been expressed.

This latter group includes many of those which under the proposed legislation will be classified as "likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction."
Physical Environments: The following is a physical description of the environment of the United States which will be impacted by restoration of species and subspecies described in the U.S. "Red Book." The "Red Book" is used to demonstrate the endangered species list as it may appear under the proposed legislation. The basis for the physical description is a discussion of the biomes of the United States with further focusing on isolated communities within those biomes. The principal biomes of the world, and their descriptions are adapted from Kendeigh (Animal Ecology, Prentice-Hall, Inc., 1961).
Following the description of the environment will be a discussion of the economic environment surrounding endangered species restoration.

Association of endangered species with biomes: The major unit in the ecological system is the biome. A biome is a biotic community, characterized by distinctiveness in life-forms of the important climax species.
